chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad all together, from Ibn Faddal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Umar ibn Aban, from al-Subah ibn Sayyabah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, a man may love you [the Shias] and not know what you are saying [in terms of belief], so Allah, Exalted and Mighty, enters him into Paradise. And indeed, a man may hate you and not know what you are saying, so Allah, Exalted and Mighty, enters him into the Fire. And indeed, a man from among you will have his record filled [with good deeds] without [him performing] any deeds. I said, 'And how can that be?' He said: 'He passes by a group who belittle us; when they see him, some of them say to others, 'Restrain yourselves, for this man is from their Shias.' And a man from our Shias passes by them, so they mock him and speak ill of him, so Allah writes for him rewards because of that, until his record is filled without [him performing] any deeds.'
ai.seo_question: How can a person's record of deeds be filled with good or bad without them performing any specific actions?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the Shia concept of 'social credit,' where divine recompense is granted for mere recognition of the Ahl al-Bayt's status, highlighting the spiritual weight of social identity. It underscores the principle that unintentional acts of deference or disrespect toward the Shia, driven by an awareness of their lineage, carry significant karmic consequences, effectively filling one's record with good deeds or sins without active ritual performance. This reflects the scholarly emphasis on the interplay between public perception and private divine accounting in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: H 14943 – Abu Ali Al-Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbaar, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad together, from Ibn Fazzaal, from Sa’albat Bin Maymoun, from Umar Bin Aban, from Al-Sabbaah Bin Sayaabat, who has said: Abu Abdullahasws has said that: ‘The man who loves you (Shites) and does not know what you are saying (believe in), so Allahazwj Enters him into the Paradise. And if the man hates you (Shites), and does not know what you are saying (believing in), so Allahazwj would Enter him into the Fire. And the man from among you would fill his book (of deeds) from without (having performed) deeds’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws, and how can that be?’ Heasws said: ‘He passed by the group belittling us, they see him, and some of them say to the others, ‘Refrain, for this man is from theirasws Shites’. And the man from ourasws Shites passes by them, so they mock him and speak (bad) regarding him, so Allahazwj Writes for him Rewards, due to that, until his book (of) deeds gets filled up without (having performed) any deeds’.
en.sarwar: 496. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Al-Jaham, from Abu Khadija who said: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said to me;

‘How much (distance is there) between you and Al-Basra?’ I said, ‘It is five (days) by the water (sea) if the wind is good, and upon the back (of the earth) eight days or approximate to that’. So he (a.s.) said: ‘This is not near. Visit each other frequently for there will not be an escape on the Day of Judgement from each human being to bring a witness who would testify for him upon his Religion’. And said: ‘If a Muslims sees his brother, it is a revival for his Religion if he Mentions Allah (azwj) (during their meeting)’.
